subject: Mid-term top-up cadence, pro-rata invoicing, and legal timing
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@quanticohealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-term top-up: requested quantity, invoicing cadence, and legal lead time

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Per our conversation youre planning to add 250k additional token capacity for the remainder of your contract term (through 2026-12-31) to cover a new triage workflow. A few points we want to align on so Sales/Finance/Legal can move quickly: 

- Top-up size: 250k token-equivalent units (we can convert to GB-hours if you prefer).
- Billing: we propose a pro-rata charge for the remainder of the term on your next monthly invoice (prorated from the effective date to 2026-12-31). Example attached.
- Credits / discount: we can offer an uplift credit schedule instead of a percent discount — details below if your procurement prefers an invoice credit vs. headline discount.
- Co-terming: if you want the top-up to co-term to 2026-12-31 we will carry the pro-rata and then annualize at renewal; if you prefer an add-on with its own 12-month start date we can accommodate.
- Legal timing: typical SOW amendment turnaround is 3-5 business days for standard terms; we can accelerate for an SLA addendum if needed.

Im attaching a draft SOW (QH_TopUp_SOW_v3.docx) and a simple invoice-proration-example.xlsx so procurement can see numbers. Please confirm: 1) you want pro-rata on next invoice, 2) you want the top-up to co-term with the current contract, and 3) procurement contact for PO/legal review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short sync if helpful.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: QH_TopUp_SOW_v3.docx (docx), invoice-proration-example.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Emma Li <emma@quanticohealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Quantico Health Procurement <procurement@quanticohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mid-term top-up: requested quantity, invoicing cadence, and legal lead time

Hi Irene —

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement: 

1) Can you send the proration math in the invoice example as a line-item-level PDF? Procurement needs it in the PO packet.
2) Is the uplift credit a one-time invoice credit or an ongoing rate reduction? They asked specifically so they can map to cost centers.
3) Our legal team (procurement@quanticohealth.com) will need to review the SOW amendment. Please include a redline-ready Word file.

Wed like to aim for the top-up on the next invoice cycle if legal can sign off within two weeks. If thats tight we may request an interim PO to lock pricing.

Emma Li
Director, Platform Integrations
Quantico Health

On Wed, Jun 10, 2026 at 09:24 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (see attached draft SOW + proration worksheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-term top-up: requested quantity, invoicing cadence, and legal lead time

Irene —

Drafting two quick options to present: 

Option A (clean invoicing):
- One-time pro-rata charge on next invoice for remainder of term (6.5 months) for 250k tokens
- Offer a one-time invoice credit equal to 10% of the top-up amount if Quantico submits PO within 5 business days
- Co-term: top-up expires 2026-12-31 (no extra renewal commitment)

Option B (commercial smoothing):
- Spread the top-up cost over remaining term (monthly amortization) with a 6% administration fee waived as a concession
- Offer a 15% credit conditional on committing to a 12-month renew/expansion at renewal
- If they'd like SOW to be standalone (12 months) we price as an add-on with full-year invoice upfront

Notes: Option A keeps finance/tax cleaner (one-line charge). Option B helps customer smooth monthly budgeting. Both can be made to co-term; we should confirm procurements preference before sending a formal quote.

If you want me to run the numbers into the spreadsheet I attached earlier I can; Ben can confirm whether the 15% conditional credit needs AE sign-off.

- Karthik
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@quanticohealth.com>, Quantico Health Procurement <procurement@quanticohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-term top-up: requested quantity, invoicing cadence, and legal lead time

Emma / Procurement —

Per Karthiks note, we have two clean commercial paths. Ive filled the proration worksheet with exact numbers for Option A and Option B and attached invoice-proration-example.xlsx. Quick summary (numbers rounded):

- Option A (one-time): $38,750 pro-rata (one-line on next invoice). 10% invoice credit ($3,875) if PO submitted within 5 business days.
- Option B (amortized): $6,150/month for the remainder of term (no up-front), 15% conditional credit tied to renewal expansion.

What procurement told us they need: PDF of line-item math, redline-ready Word SOW, PO contact and expected PO date. Ive attached the line-item worksheet and a redline-friendly SOW draft (QH_TopUp_SOW_v3.docx).

If procurement confirms they prefer the one-time charge and can accept the SOW within standard terms, we can schedule the change for the 2026-06-30 invoice. If they need >10 business days for legal, well keep the pricing and schedule it for the following cycle.

Open to a 20-minute call to finalize the path.

Thanks —
Irene

Attachments: invoice-proration-example.xlsx (xlsx), QH_TopUp_SOW_v3.docx (docx)
From: Quantico Health Procurement <procurement@quanticohealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Emma Li <emma@quanticohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mid-term top-up: requested quantity, invoicing cadence, and legal lead time

Irene / Emma —

Thanks for the options. A couple items from our side: 

- Please send the proration math as a flattened PDF line-item (not spreadsheet) for PO packet.
- Well need a redline of the SOW (Word) with the clause for data residency and audit rights clearly called out.
- Legals requested turnaround is 7-10 business days for any amendments requiring data/residency language. If you can flag any standard text weve already accepted previously it will speed review.

For timeline planning: we can commit to Option A (one-time pro-rata) if the PO is in by 6/24. If PO slips past that wed need the amortization option or a short-term PO to hold pricing.

Procurement
Quantico Health
